findings.quote: | "already runs Kubernetes, minimal code changes" | Amazon EKS | [deploy Kubernetes-compatible applications without refactoring](../facts/eks.md#eks-certified-kubernetes-conformant) | no Kubernetes skills: Amazon ECS |
findings.evidence: The guard cannot apply: a stem that says the company 'already runs Kubernetes' has Kubernetes skills by definition, so 'no Kubernetes skills' never meets this signal. The guard that does decide real stems is location: 'the clusters must stay in the company's own data center: Amazon EKS Anywhere' (the twin line of q009 already uses it, fact eks-faq-anywhere-clusters-run-entirely-on-your-infrastructure), or 'the company wants to leave Kubernetes and keep the least to operate: Amazon ECS'.
findings.resolution: fix-19: the 'But not if' cell now reads 'clusters stay in the data center: EKS Anywhere'.

findings.section: Signals and traps; Recap from memory (Recap 2)
findings.quote: | a reliable connection: EKS Hybrid Nodes |
findings.evidence: The guard implies that EKS Anywhere is wrong whenever the site has a reliable connection. The chapter itself says the opposite: 2-services.md says EKS Anywhere 'runs connected to an AWS Region or disconnected from it'. Fact eks-hybrid-nodes-need-reliable-connection says only that Hybrid Nodes need a connection ('must have a reliable connection'); it does not say that a connection rules out EKS Anywhere. EKS Hybrid Nodes is not among the chapter's services or the exam guide's in-scope services (registry show 19: ECR, ECS, ECS Anywhere, EKS, EKS Anywhere, EKS Distro, Fargate). Recap 2 drills this guard. The guard that decides is who runs the control plane: 'AWS must run the control plane, nodes on premises: EKS Hybrid Nodes'. Alternatively, contrast with ECS Anywhere, which is in scope.
findings.resolution: fix-19: the 'But not if' cell and the Recap 2 answer now read 'AWS runs the control plane: EKS Hybrid Nodes'. The EKS Anywhere card in 2-services.md now says what Hybrid Nodes are: '[AWS manages the AWS-hosted Kubernetes control plane], your servers join as nodes, and the site [must have a reliable connection]'.

findings.quote: - Change the task placement strategy of the service to binpack on memory, so that the tasks fill as few instances as possible.
findings.evidence: Half of the key of q012 is the binpack placement strategy, and one distractor turns on the target capacity of managed scaling (50 versus 100 percent, fact ecs-target-capacity-below-100-keeps-spare-instances). Neither is taught: 2-deep.md never mentions task placement strategies (binpack, spread) or target capacity. The Review link points to the subsection 'Service auto scaling changes the task count and capacity providers supply the compute', which does not contain them. Add two sentences on placement strategies and target capacity to that subsection (facts ecs-placement-binpack-least-unused-cpu-memory, ecs-placement-strategy-types-binpack-random-spread, ecs-target-capacity-below-100-keeps-spare-instances).
findings.resolution: fix-19: step 3 of the scaling subsection now adds 'Binpack placement [minimizes the number of container instances in use](ecs-placement-binpack-least-unused-cpu-memory).' The target capacity sentence was drafted and linted but dropped for the 2,400-word cap of 2-deep.md; the q012 option d why still teaches it (ecs-target-capacity-below-100-keeps-spare-instances).

findings.quote: Create an ECR pull through cache rule for Docker Hub, store the Docker Hub credentials in a Secrets Manager secret, and use the cached images.
findings.evidence: The key has two parts, but the explanation grounds only the cache rule. Nothing in the Why, in 2-deep.md 'Go deeper: caching images', or in 1-fast.md says why the Secrets Manager secret is needed. The verified fact ecr-pull-through-cache-upstream-registries-auth says that Docker Hub (with other upstream registries) needs 'authentication with an AWS Secrets Manager secret', while ECR Public, the Kubernetes registry and Quay need none. Link it in the Why and add one sentence to the Go deeper block. Otherwise a reader who meets a stem with ECR Public as the upstream registry will wrongly add a secret.
findings.resolution: fix-19: the q006 Why now says 'The Secrets Manager secret holds the Docker Hub credentials that the rule signs in with.' (explanation only; key unchanged). findings.quote: Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy to both the task role and the task execution role that the task definition names.

The option is the violates-qualifier distractor that Q108 requires at difficulty 2. Logged for the next revision of the pair (use the access-key-in-environment-variable misconception from brief slot 1).

findings.section: Choose it or not: Fargate or EC2 capacity or Lambda
findings.quote: **Deciding question:** Does the job end within minutes, and does the team want to manage instances?
findings.evidence: The table has two rows, and neither separates Fargate from EC2 capacity on what real stems use. 'Longest run?' gives 'no hard limit' for Fargate and 'Until the task stops' for EC2, which is the same answer. The deciding question joins two questions. Exam stems choose EC2 capacity for GPUs, privileged containers or host access (facts fargate-faq-gpu-not-supported, fargate-no-privileged-containers, ecs-faq-ec2-root-access-to-os) and for large price-optimized fleets (ecs-ec2-capacity-large-workloads-price-optimized). The Signals table and speak item s02 already use these facts. Add a row 'Needs GPUs, privileged mode or host access?' and end with one question: 'Does the workload need the host or a GPU? If yes, EC2 capacity. If not, does one run end within 15 minutes? If yes, Lambda.'
findings.resolution: fix-19: the deciding question now reads 'Does it need a GPU or the host, or end within minutes?', which separates EC2 capacity (GPU or host) from Lambda (minutes) and leaves Fargate for the rest. The extra row was not added: the fast file is at 999 of 1,000 words, and the Lambda cell of a GPU row would need a fact the canon does not hold. The Signals row 1 'But not if' already says 'GPUs or privileged mode: EC2 capacity'.

findings.section: A task definition gives the agent one role and the application another
findings.quote: 3. **Pull and log.** The **task execution role** [grants the Amazon ECS container and Fargate agents](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-task-execution-role-for-agents) permission to pull from [an Amazon ECR private repository](../facts/ecs.md#ecs-task-execution-role-use-cases).
findings.evidence: The section teaches that the execution role pulls images and sends logs, but not its third common job: reading the secrets that the task definition references. The linked fact ecs-task-execution-role-use-cases names it: a task 'whose task definition references sensitive data using Secrets Manager secrets or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameters'. 'Inject a database password from Secrets Manager into the container' is a frequent exam stem, and the key is the execution role, not the task role. Without this case, the chapter's rule 'code uses the task role' leads her to the wrong role.
findings.resolution: fix-19: step 3 now reads '... permission to pull from [an Amazon ECR private repository](ecs-task-execution-role-use-cases), send logs, and read secrets.' (the linked fact names the Secrets Manager case). 1-fast Check 1 now drills it: 'A task definition passes a database password from Secrets Manager. Which role reads the secret?' with the answer linked to [references sensitive data using Secrets Manager secrets].

Logged for the orchestrator as a candidate for the next question round (suggested facts as in the finding). The FAQ quick-fire item 4 and card c008 keep the air-gapped contrast.

findings.section: Fargate gives each task its own isolated compute and no instance to manage
findings.quote: Fargate gives [20 GiB](../facts/fargate.md#fargate-faq-ephemeral-storage-20-gib-erased) of **ephemeral** (ih-FEM-er-ul) storage, erased when the task stops.
findings.evidence: The linked fact fargate-faq-ephemeral-storage-20-gib-erased has qualifiers default_or_max 'default' and adjustable true. Its claim continues: 'this ephemeral storage volume can be expanded up to 200GiB on Amazon ECS and 175 GiB on Amazon EKS.' Without 'by default' the trap reads as a fixed size, and she will reject a correct option such as 'increase the ephemeral storage of the task definition' for a large temporary file. Write 'by default' (the A-list row already says 'Default ephemeral storage').
findings.resolution: fix-19: the trap now reads 'Fargate gives [20 GiB] of **ephemeral** (ih-FEM-er-ul) storage by default, erased when the task stops.'

findings.quote: Add an Auto Scaling group capacity provider with managed scaling to the capacity provider strategy of the service, with a target capacity of 50 percent to keep spare instances.

findings.section: In awsvpc mode each task gets its own network interface
findings.quote: **Spot the bug.** Fargate tasks in private subnets with no NAT gateway have interface endpoints for the ECR API and the Docker registry. The image pull fails. Why?
findings.evidence: The cut of containers-q007 (verified, not ready) leaves the awsvpc and private-pull subsection, its Signals row 'private subnets with no internet access, images in Amazon ECR' and the trap containers-trap-instance-target-type without a shipped question. These are common stems for 'privately' and 'no internet access'. If a question is swapped (see exam-01), prefer keeping either q007 or q011 over a second item on the same concept.
findings.resolution: fix-19: both q007 and q011 now ship (see exam-01); q003 and q010 were moved out instead.
